speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) how has COVID-19 affected low-income Singaporean and transnational families, low-income seniors, the differently-abled, and persons with mental health conditions; (b) how does the Ministry monitor and assess the COVID-19 impact on these Singaporeans; (c) what measures, including multi-Ministry efforts, are being put in place to support them comprehensively; and (d) how has the COVID-19 crisis illuminated opportunities to review existing social support policies for these groups in terms of food security, job security and personal resources for "rainy" days.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some groups inadvertently feel the impact more immediately and more acutely.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, low-income workers with little savings may need additional financial help if their work is affected.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Others with unique care needs, such as persons with limited mobility or disabilities, may worry if services such as meal delivery or home nursing would be disrupted during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Though we have temporarily halted activities at Senior Activity Centres as added precaution for our seniors, the centres’ staff continue to watch over the seniors within their service boundaries and check in on them remotely where necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, MSF and other Government agencies have stepped up measures to address various needs arising from COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have made the application process more convenient by allowing them to submit their documents electronically.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also work with the People’s Association to provide other forms of help, such as assistance buying food and groceries, if the person under quarantine or Stay-Home Notice does not have any such support from their families, neighbours, or other parties.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Silver Generation Office reaches out to vulnerable seniors such as those living alone or who are frail.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Since February 2020, Silver Generation Ambassadors have started visiting these seniors in their homes to communicate COVID-19 precautionary measures, such as hygiene tips and social distancing.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They also identify seniors who require additional assistance during this period, and link them up with the appropriate social service agencies and service providers to ensure that their needs are met.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: During the upcoming circuit breaker, these agencies will continue to reach out to our seniors through the various forms.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, the Finance Minister recently announced our second care and support package to help Singaporeans tide over the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For individuals who require employment assistance, Workforce Singapore (WSG) and NTUC’s Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) offer a range of employment facilitation services and programmes under the Adapt and Grow initiative.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are also continuing our efforts to make social services and help more convenient, comprehensive and coordinated.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, in the area of food insecurity, we have convened a multi-sector workgroup comprising food organisations, volunteer groups and Government agencies to address issues of food waste and distribution inefficiencies.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Members of the workgroup are supporting one another, especially during this period, to keep their operations going, highlighting the spirit of partnership that serves us well in times like this.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Such partnerships complement ongoing efforts and schemes such as ComCare that assist low-income households with daily living expenses including food, and MOE’s Financial Assistance Scheme for school-going children in lower income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has also underscored the importance of a whole-of-society approach to tackling crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We see an outpouring of support from corporates, unions, volunteer groups, grassroots and religious groups to support the vulnerable.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many have also donated generously to The Courage Fund to support our healthcare and frontline workers, and lower income families affected by COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These are just some of the examples of many instances of the community rallying to support one another.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And this is especially important, because caring for one another, especially the vulnerable, is not simply a collective responsibility, but a national imperative during crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond cushioning the economic impact, it is also about sustaining relationships and strengthening our social capital as a collective.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: COVID-19 may have brought challenges for us, but this is also an opportunity for us to strengthen our bonds and build a stronger society.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I have three supplementary questions, if you do not mind.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: With the new circuit breaker measures, given the closure of Family Violence Specialist Centres and Child Protection Specialist Centres, with limited provision of services, what is the Ministry's plan to ensure that individuals in need of support for such issues continue to receive adequate and timely support, especially given that these centres serve as essential safe spaces for these individuals?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The second one is do the MSF services for this issue, such as Adult Protection Services and Child Protection Services, have adequate resources to deal with the potential increase in abuse, violence cases that may increase as individuals now spend a significant amount of time at home and have less access to other possible safe spaces?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: And will the Minister actually have these services introduce measures to allow individuals in distress to walk in to a safe space?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The last supplementary question is I think this crisis, which has caught us off guard, also shown a spotlight on the frontline role of social service agencies (SSAs) and ground-ups who know the needs of the affected communities better and also get to them better.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I just want to ask the Minister, I understand there is a lot of anxiety amongst these SSAs and ground-ups, especially the smaller ones, particularly in terms of donations drying up, so could the Minister share with the House what are some of the support measures that we will have for them?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, during the circuit breaker, we have looked at what is happening in other countries which have imposed these kinds of measures to keep people indoors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is a trend we are observing of higher rates of domestic violence and quarrels, and friction in the family.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Family Violence Specialist Centres, the Child Protection Specialist Centres, these are essential services.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In terms of the social sector, we entirely recognise the concerns they have had.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, both MSF and the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) have been having dialogue sessions and town halls, both in person and digitally, electronically with the SSAs, to understand their specific concerns and to help them through this period.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, of course, subsequently, in this Budget debate, we will be announcing further measures to support our SSAs.
